title: Towards a machine-learning assisted non-invasive classification of dengue severity using wearable PPG data: a prospective clinical study.
summary: Random forest, MLP/SVM and time-frequency CNN models classify dengue severity from wearable continuous PPG segments; five-fold cross-validation evaluates models. Prospective Vietnamese clinical dataset: 132 adults recruited, 127 after signal-quality filtering (1,223 hours), and 15 children in secondary acute-vs-follow-up analysis. Models classified clinical severity; best adult RF accuracy about .69 baseline and time-frequency CNN improved metrics by >8%, final accuracy .78; pediatric distinction accuracy .89. This supports physiological signal association and feasibility, not a validated triage device. Prospective observational cohort, but internal 5-fold CV on small single-site Vietnamese population; paper notes homogeneous cohort and need for broader validation. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.
